findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, assigning it a public network endpoint. Although the shown security group ingress is VPC-scoped, this unnecessarily exposes the database to public-network reachability if security-group rules change or are added.

The RDS instance explicitly sets storage_encrypted = false, leaving database storage and snapshots unencrypted at rest. An unauthorized party obtaining underlying storage or a snapshot could access database contents.

The EC2 application role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on every resource. Compromise of the application instance would yield broad control over S3, EC2, and RDS resources rather than only the permissions required by the application.

MySQL port 3306 is allowed from the entire VPC CIDR rather than only the application security group or required hosts. Any workload or compromised host in the VPC can attempt to connect to the database.

The database password is interpolated into EC2 user data and written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. User data is retrievable through the instance metadata service by processes on the instance and is commonly exposed through instance-management access, increasing the chance that the database credential is disclosed.
